title: Blood test for children
what: A nurse takes a little blood from your child's fingertip or a vein. It usually takes a couple of minutes.
why: At a checkup, during illness, before kindergarten or school, before surgery, or to check treatment.
duration: usually 3 to 10 minutes; results often come in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: If your child has fainted or is very afraid of needles
If your child is allergic to latex or bandages
If your child has a bleeding disorder

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Babies are usually fed as normal. Ask first. Older children are often asked to come fasting. Ask the lab how many hours without food.

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: Plain water is usually fine. It helps keep your child calmer.

prepare.title: Mindset
prepare.text: Tell your child the truth: a quick prick, a little pain, and you will be right there. Do not use the doctor as a threat.

prepare.title: Bring along
prepare.text: A favorite toy and a treat for afterward.

bring: A toy and a snack for afterward
steps: You sit and hold your child on your lap, as the nurse shows you
The finger or arm is wiped with antiseptic
From a finger: a quick prick and a few drops into a tube
From a vein: a band, a quick prick, and blood fills a tube
A cotton pad is pressed on the spot, and your child is praised
feel: A quick prick. Your child may cry, and that is normal
Your calm helps your child a lot
after: Press the cotton pad for a few minutes
Praise your child right away and give a snack if they were fasting
Results usually come in 1 to 2 days

faq.q: Why is blood taken from a vein and not a finger?
faq.a: Many tests need more blood. A vein is faster and more accurate.

faq.q: How can I calm my child?
faq.a: Be honest and calm, hold them on your lap, and distract them with a toy or a cartoon.

reminders.text: Your child's blood test is tomorrow. Check if fasting is needed, and bring a toy and a snack.
